units.translation: On ⟦1⟧, where the common ⟦2⟧ is attached only to the second member, cf. ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧.
neither to be strong nor to be able to move
so that neither of the gods nor any of men

⟦1⟧ (⟦2⟧, otherwise unattested) ⟦3⟧ Hesych.; on ⟦4⟧ the scholiast notes: ⟦5⟧· ⟦6⟧, cf. Timaeus, Lexicon Platonicum: ⟦7⟧· ⟦8⟧. Here there is serious confusion: at ⟦9⟧ it is said of young children and young animals that at first they ⟦10⟧, then ⟦11⟧, ⟦12⟧. The scholion on that passage again agrees with ours, but clearly ⟦13⟧ = ⟦14⟧, ⟦15⟧, to stand upright, ⟦16⟧, and so this one continues: ⟦17⟧ “⟦18⟧” ⟦19⟧ (not ⟦20⟧), ⟦21⟧. Is this, as Ruhnken (Tim. p. 21) thinks, our passage? A woman was speaking (⟦22⟧), but the quotation would be very inaccurate, and so this is listed as a separate fragment, 416 Ddf. Ruhnken collects further material from the lexicographers; there were still more attestations for this word family, and so also in Odyssey ⟦23⟧ 3 (⟦24⟧) the old and probably correct reading was ⟦25⟧ or ⟦26⟧. Fortunately the meaning is beyond doubt.
it also means to exult and to leap disorderly
to exult and to leap disorderly
whenever he moves himself most quickly
as if I am no longer able to raise myself

According to the scholion, the Pythia comes out ⟦1⟧ (like the blinded Polymestor ⟦2⟧, Stanl.), which modern scholars are unwilling to believe; they even explain it as propping her hands on a staff. The words admit no explanation other than that of the scholion, except that one can understand them as narrative (as at ⟦3⟧); in particular ⟦4⟧ points to this: she crawled like a small child, ⟦5⟧. Cf. the riddle of the Sphinx: the child is actually four-footed, the old man only three-footed. So also ⟦6⟧ (here = ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧, cf. ⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧) is a certain intensification (⟦11⟧, ⟦12⟧. ⟦13⟧ etc.) of ⟦14⟧, and the very fine conjecture of Herwerden ⟦15⟧, ⟦16⟧ is not needed; cf. also (Paley) ⟦17⟧ ⟦18⟧.
who has not yet raised himself
a woman left alone is nothing; there is no Ares in her
⟦1⟧ (and ⟦2⟧), because she is trying to flee as quickly as possible; with ⟦3⟧ (Homer B 792) ⟦4⟧ Weckl. compares 915 ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧, 729 ⟦8⟧.
